description: Team Tech Trivonix is a team of four passionate and innovative minds participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We aim to combine creativity, technology, and problem-solving to develop impactful solutions inspired by real-world challenges and space exploration. Our team believes in collaboration, innovation, and turning ideas into meaningful solutions.
summary:
LUNA-SCOPE is a lunar landing-site analysis and decision-support prototype developed by Team TechTrivonix for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps mission planners compare potential lunar landing locations by evaluating sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and terrain characteristics.

The project uses NASA JPL Horizons to calculate the Sun's and Earth's azimuth and elevation, along with seven-day visibility estimates. It uses NASA LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) Digital Elevation Models to analyze lunar surface elevation and terrain slope.

The backend is developed using Python and FastAPI, while the interactive dashboard uses Streamlit and Plotly to display environmental indicators, terrain measurements, and landing-site comparisons.

A preliminary weighted scoring model combines sunlight, Earth visibility, terrain slope, and elevation variation to generate a suitability score for each location.

The goal is to provide a visual, data-driven tool that supports lunar landing-site evaluation and helps identify locations with potentially favourable environmental and terrain conditions.

Team Tech Trivonix : Prashant (Backend), Anant (Frontend), Praveen (AI/ML), and Sakshi (Research).
details:
LUNA-SCOPE is a project developed by our team, TECHTRIVONIX, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our main idea is to make it easier to identify and compare suitable landing locations on the Moon.

The project provides an interactive dashboard where users can explore different lunar landing sites and understand important factors such as sunlight availability, Earth visibility, terrain slope and overall site suitability.

One of the main features we are developing is Terrain-Aware Horizon Analysis. Sometimes the Sun or Earth may be above the geometric horizon, but nearby mountains or crater rims can block the actual view. Our system aims to identify these obstructions and show which directions have a clearer view. It will also provide a 360-degree view of the surrounding terrain.

We are using Python, Streamlit and Plotly for the frontend and visualizations. Our planned backend uses FastAPI, NumPy and Rasterio. For data, we are working with NASA's LOLA lunar elevation data and JPL Horizons.

What makes LUNA-SCOPE different is that it combines terrain analysis and astronomical visibility in one platform instead of looking at these factors separately.

While developing the project, we considered terrain elevation, slope, sunlight conditions, Earth visibility, data accuracy and the challenges of working with lunar surface data.

Our aim is to help make lunar landing-site evaluation easier to understand and support better-informed decisions for future lunar exploration missions.
